category_title: Students who use physical presence and threats to intimidate faculty
minimal_context: The student arrives in the classroom during general instruction and confronts the professor in front of the other students.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Good morning everyone. Please take your seats so we can begin today's lecture.

STUDENT: (Slams textbook on the desk and refuses to return to his seat, standing in a power stance looking down to communicate dominance) I'm not sitting down.

TUTOR: I need you to go to your seat now.

STUDENT: (Uses a 'size up and down' nonverbal look at the professor) No.

TUTOR: We can discuss any issues after class. Let's move on.

STUDENT: (Yells out to the class) She is the worst teacher in the world! Don't pay attention to anything she says. She's stupid.

options.A: Progressively and methodically tune the student's awareness to each body part, followed by intentionally relaxing each part of the body from their toes to the top of their head.
options.B: Place extra emphasis on classroom decorum and participation by increasing the overall point value associated with discussion and guiding the students through an exercise to establish classroom rules.
options.C: Provide the student with access to similar, but more socially appropriate, sensory stimulation by giving them a squishy, stress-relief ball to use during the lecture.
options.D: Provide a clear beginning and end for each instructional task and activity presented during the lecture, maintaining this consistent structure throughout the remainder of the course.
